newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metro Pacific plans to hike stake in Smart.
newsitem.headline: Metro Pacific plans to hike stake in Smart.

text.p: Metro Pacific Corp (MPC), the local flagship unit of First Pacific Co Ltd, said on Monday it is considering raising its equity interest in Smart Communications Inc from the current 35 percent.
This would involve the issuance of new common shares of MPC in consideration of the increased shareholdings in Smart, Metro Pacific said in a statement.
"It's going to be a significant increase from where we are now," Seumas Gallacher, the company's executive director, told Reuters.
He said the details of the increased stake is still being worked out.
MPC and parent First Pacific each own 35 percent of Smart. Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Co has a 15 percent stake and the rest are held by individual shareholders.

"The prospective higher level of ownership in Smart will raise MPC's investment in telecommunications; thereby providing a better balance in MPC' investment portfolio in terms of risks, recurring income and cash flow, and growth prospects," MPC said.
MPC's other principal businesses are also in property, consumer products, packaging and banking.
Gallacher said Smart planned to sell 20 to 25 percent of its equity to the public in June.
It posted a net income of 255 million in 1996.
The company had said it is spending 15 billion pesos in the next two years for its expansion programme that will double the size of its cellular network and extend its basic telephone network.
The expansion plans will result in 450 total cell sites, and six cellular switches. Its total cellular network is now at over 250 cell sites.
Aside from its mobile phone business, Smart is building its basic telephone network and also operates an international gateway facility and a paging service.
Smart is mandated to install a total of 700,000 landlines by the end of 1997 in exchange for its cellular phone and international gateway facility permits.
